# 06 - Harness integration

Each inference node selects its harness through `config.harness`, defaulting to `codex`.
Loop settings supply per-harness model and effort defaults; loop-level harness input is rejected.
Decision routes and temporary boolean predicates use the Codex decider; structured repair uses the structured-completion port. See
[ADR-0019](decisions/ADR-0019-inference-node-harness.md) and
[ADR-0023](decisions/ADR-0023-installed-claude-code.md).

## Native Chat workflow integration (#443)

Native Chat is an entry point into the existing engine, not a second inference implementation.
The gateway seeds one system loop with **Trigger → Inference → Context mutation → Exit**. It uses normal harness
selection, model/effort defaults and readiness checks. The inference captures plain text; the
ordinary Context mutation constructs the exact response envelope deterministically.
Seeding and device pairing make no provider request and do not silently choose a discovered model.
Each turn pins the published definition and effective defaults through native admission.
Missing CLI/authentication/model prerequisites produce actionable readiness before a new turn is
admitted; there is no substitute reply or provider failover.
The minimal system seed can exist published before model setup; it cannot send until ready.

The seeded inference node starts a fresh session in a temporary working directory. Its prompt
receives the current text and server-built bounded conversation history. The existing harness
policy applies: [ADR-0063](decisions/ADR-0063-loop-turns-without-personal-extensions.md) is amended
by [ADR-0067](decisions/ADR-0067-codex-inherits-configured-plugins.md), so Codex inherits configured
plugins and their tools/services while standalone MCP discovery and other isolation defaults remain.
Owners may edit the workflow's interior, including its harness, prompt, model, effort,
scripts, decisions and awaited subloops. Native Chat does not sandbox arbitrary owner-authored
Script commands or introduce a smart-home routing provider. Guided transcription is an ordinary
Script normalizer described below.

The loop boundary uses the canonical `graphgoblin.chat.v1` input schema from
`packages/contracts/src/chat.ts`. The server supplies `conversationId`, `requestId`, turn counter,
current input and recent valid history. A text input is `{kind: 'text', text}`. An audio input is
`{kind: 'audio', audio: {id, mimeType, bytes, path}, caption?}`; only the server can resolve the private
absolute path. A client sends an upload id, never a path or URL. The server limits history to the
most recent twelve valid completed turn pairs and 64,000 characters, dropping oldest whole pairs.

The boundary requires one manual trigger named `chat-input`, exposed to exactly UI and API, and
the canonical `chatResponse` variable schema. The deterministic Context mutation writes the
response into `/vars/chatResponse`. Every successful exit returns exactly `vars.chatResponse` to
exactly the caller. Failure/exhausted exits may return none or that same canonical response; they
never become successful assistant messages. The public response is exactly
`{protocol: 'graphgoblin.chat.v1', reply: '<nonblank text>'}`. Strings, `text`, `message` and arbitrary
JSON are not reply aliases. The chat projection validates a successful native result again on
read, so an invalid result is `CHAT_RESPONSE_INVALID` without a reply or future-history entry.

Draft saves refuse changes to the locked trigger identity/type/exposure/canonical schema and the
`chatResponse` variable schema. Other boundary wiring issues remain saveable and block
publication/admission. A generic system-loop start, draft test or Subloop accepts text-only
protocol input, even when its published loop supports audio. Only native chat admission resolves
a new audio reference. Verified immutable native replay may retain the source audio; a new start
or caller-supplied replay id cannot grant path authority.

### Configure an audio normalizer

Audio is unavailable in the default text-only loop. To enable it, replace the trigger input schema
with the exported canonical audio-capable schema and make `chat-normalize` the only node directly
after `chat-input`. Use one of these native node configurations:

| Node    | Required configuration                                                                       | Recorded text                                                                                 |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Script  | `stdin: 'thread'`, `stdout: 'last-output'`; return JSON `{text}`                             | `thread.outputs['chat-normalize'].value.text`                                                 |
| Subloop | `output.mode: 'result-only'`, `output.resultTo.lastOutput: true`; the child returns `{text}` | `thread.outputs['chat-normalize'].value.result.text`, with its envelope `status: 'succeeded'` |

Successful Script output continues to the protected check. Unhandled exit codes fail normally;
an existing explicit exit-code mapping to `out` retains its native meaning.

The normalizer must handle text pass-through as well as audio transcription. The protected chain
is `chat-input.out → chat-normalize.out → chat-normalize-check`: the canonical expression decision
continues through `valid` into the authored workflow or through `invalid` into the failure exit
`chat-normalize-invalid` (`outcome: 'failure'`, `returns: 'none'`, no destinations). Input, normalizer
and check cannot be revisited or bypassed; the failure exit accepts only that invalid edge.
The check validates the original recorded Script object or succeeded Subloop result before a
later model/action runs. It requires exactly one key, `text`, whose nonblank string is at most
16,000 UTF-16 code units. Unknown fields, blank/overlength text and a malformed Subloop envelope
fail without continuing to later actions. Expression errors fail safely too; no coercion/repair
changes transcript content.

Use the domain's `enableChatAudio(definition, normalizer)` and `disableChatAudio(definition)`
helpers to change the canonical trigger/normalizer/check/failure chain as one edit. Enabling refuses
ambiguous continuation wiring and reserved-id collisions. Disabling can also remove a partial
chain: it uses exactly one valid existing check continuation, or requires an explicit
`{continuationNodeId}` naming an ordinary nontrigger step (`SYSTEM_CHAT_CONTINUATION_REQUIRED`).
It removes reserved voice nodes/incident edges and existing trigger-outgoing edges, restores one
trigger continuation and leaves other ordinary nodes/edges intact. For the exact untouched seed prompt,
they also switch its input reference; they do not rewrite arbitrary owner prompts. Custom
interiors must consume the recorded normalized text described above. Subloops already await their
child; do not add a `wait` property or change the native subloop result envelope. The projector
selects the extractor from the pinned node kind and independently validates the recorded value.
The owner editor exposes these edits as **Set up voice messages**, **Add voice steps** and
**Turn off voice messages**. Setup stages a real Script/Subloop configuration without executing
it; publication remains a separate action.

The normalized text must contain 1–16,000 nonblank UTF-16 code units. For an audio turn, a successful raw
run without a valid recorded normalizer result becomes `CHAT_AUDIO_NORMALIZATION_INVALID` and
does not display a reply or enter future history. A model-generated guess is never a transcript.
The session's **Configured by loop** state establishes this static contract only: an unavailable
executable or malformed external result still fails at runtime. The guided preset adds tested
Whisper.cpp and OpenAI routes; arbitrary custom normalizers remain the owner’s responsibility.
There is no browser speech-recognition fallback or speech synthesis.

Audio files live in the private `<dataDir>/chat-audio/` directory and retain their bytes for the
owner's normalizer. Unused uploads expire after one hour. Consumed files remain available while
the linked native run/history can reference them and are cleaned up with history ownership,
preserving restart recovery. They are not artifacts encoded into event text or publicly served
files. Retained used/unused/in-flight audio is capped at 64 MiB per audience and 256 MiB per gateway;
exceeding the quota refuses an upload without deleting referenced inputs. Deletion of one turn
does not retroactively erase its text from later immutable native histories. See
[the Chat frontend](09-frontend-and-pwa.md#native-chat-and-the-goblin-pwa-443) and
[ADR-0065](decisions/ADR-0065-native-chat-system-loops-and-device-pairing.md).

### Plain text capture and context admission (ADR-0068)

`output.capture: 'text'` preserves `finalText` exactly as a string, including JSON-looking answers.
It cannot be combined with an output schema. Leaving this optional field unset is equivalent to
`auto`, retaining strict existing
JSON/schema validation for other workflows; malformed structured output is never salvaged by
selecting a convenient object. The standard chat seed uses text capture and an editable 300-second
inference deadline. Existing published loops are not rewritten when the seed changes; reads keep
omitted capture fields and their existing draft tokens unchanged.

Ollama admission budgets the complete rendered prompt, model wrapper and output reserve before
sending it. Only recognized standard chat prompts may omit oldest complete history pairs. The
stored input/history stays intact and the turn exposes retained/omitted counts. Custom prompts
are never truncated. Required input that cannot fit is refused before dispatch with
`INFERENCE_CONTEXT_LIMIT`; unknown context profiles produce `INFERENCE_CONTEXT_UNSUPPORTED`.

The initial qualified profile is deliberately narrow: Ollama 0.32.15, Qwen3.5 with the observed
GPT-2/Qwen35 byte tokenizer, the unmodified single-user renderer, no preset system/messages and
`none` effort. Its allocation is at most 4096 tokens, with a 1024-token reply reserve, a 512-token
wrapper allowance and a conservative UTF-8 byte ceiling for prompt/schema input. This is not an
exact tokenizer count or the model’s advertised maximum. Other discovered models remain visible
with an unsupported/unverified reason until their profile is qualified; discovery, readiness and
dispatch share the same policy. Enabled choices/defaults are preserved. Requalification is required
when the runtime/profile changes; discovery alone is not memory or performance evidence.

### Guided voice preset (ADR-0068)

Settings → Voice saves gateway-owned configuration with revision checks. A pure preview adds the
ordinary `graphgoblin-voice-normalize` Script with a non-secret configuration snapshot; explicit
staging checks the reviewed configuration revision and loop draft hash atomically. Publishing is
separate. Device clones are listed individually. A custom normalizer is opened for manual review,
never overwritten. An editor handoff refuses dirty/restored/conflicting drafts, pauses autosave
while staging and preserves Undo after the saved baseline changes.

Local transcription uses a separately qualified Whisper.cpp executable and a verified small
English model. The guided downloader installs only immutable allowlisted model bytes, with exact
size/SHA-256, disk bounds and atomic publication; it does not install a compiler, runtime or ffmpeg.
Runtime/dependency qualification is server-owned private evidence, not a browser claim or a
version-string check. Unsupported machines can use the guided cloud connection. The setup test
transcribes a short public speech sample, records latency and unused-memory telemetry and expires its
result; changing runtime/model/configuration requires another test. Test while the usual Ollama
model is running before relying on local coexistence.

The cloud adapter uses a dedicated `voice.openai.*` secret and OpenAI transcription. Setup names
provider billing and requires acknowledgement before uploading the public sample. The chosen route
is disclosed before Send and pinned before transcription. Auto prefers a suitable local route;
cloud is used only when explicitly configured/permitted. A failed or uncertain dispatch never
silently fails over to another provider or retries a command. Text needs neither route. Caption
text precedes the transcript, and the protected canonical `{text}` check validates the combined
input before inference or other workflow actions.

## The harness port (Decided)

```ts
interface HarnessPort {
  id: 'codex' | 'claude' | 'ollama'; // LiteLLM is a recorded later adapter idea
  preflight(): Promise<{
    state: HarnessReadinessState;
    ok: boolean;
    version?: string;
    authenticated?: boolean;
    problems: string[];
    authMethod?: 'claude.ai' | null;
    supportedPolicies?: ClaudePolicy[];
    models?: ClaudeModelCapability[];
  }>;
  start(req: HarnessStartRequest, signal: AbortSignal): HarnessSession;
  resume(sessionId: string, req: HarnessStartRequest, signal: AbortSignal): HarnessSession;
}

type HarnessStartRequest = {
  workingDirectory: string;
  model?: string;
  effort?: Effort;
  options: InferenceConfig['harnessOptions'];
  capabilities?: InferenceConfig['capabilities'];
  turn: HarnessTurnRequest;
};
type HarnessTurnRequest = { prompt: string; outputSchema?: JsonSchema };

interface HarnessSession {
  sessionId: Promise<string>; // resolves as soon as the harness reports it
  events: AsyncIterable<HarnessEvent>; // normalised, see below
  result: Promise<HarnessResult>;
  cancel(): Promise<void>;
}

type HarnessEvent =
  | { type: 'session'; sessionId: string; mode: 'fresh' | 'resumed' }
  | { type: 'item'; item: HarnessItem } // message, reasoning summary, command, file change, tool call, search
  | { type: 'usage'; inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; cached?: number }
  | {
      type: 'submitted';
      marker:
        | 'claude.assistant'
        | 'claude.result'
        | 'codex.turn.started'
        | 'ollama.response'
        | 'fake.accepted';
    }
  | { type: 'turn-complete' }
  | {
      type: 'error';
      code: string;
      message: string;
      retriable: boolean;
      submission: PromptSubmission;
    };

type HarnessResult = {
  finalText: string;
  structured?: unknown;
  usage: Usage;
  items: HarnessItem[];
};
```

Adapters translate native events into this model. The engine never sees SDK types.

## Native Ollama and discovered models (#443)

Ollama is a native Inference harness implemented in `packages/infrastructure/src/ollama/` through
the Node HTTP transport. It calls `/api/chat` directly with the exact selected model identifier,
the already-rendered prompt as one user message, streaming enabled and the node's JSON Schema
when present. It uses no CLI, OpenAI compatibility shim, external SDK or standalone chat worker.
The existing engine still owns prompt/context transforms, structured-output validation,
transcripts, usage, cancellation and recovery. Ollama is an Inference option; generic LLM
decision evaluation and structured repair retain their existing provider contracts.

### Connect and discover

One gateway-wide connection supplies the gateway-wide model catalog. Configure its origin and
enabled state in Settings. Before a saved connection exists, the defaults are
`GG_OLLAMA_ENABLED=true` and `GG_OLLAMA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434`; a saved connection takes
precedence. An origin may use HTTP or HTTPS and must contain no credentials, query, fragment or
path beyond `/`. The owner may select a local/LAN service or a trusted proxy; not every selected
server or model is necessarily local. GraphGoblin does not install/start Ollama, forward its
management key, manage proxy credentials or download/pull models.
Services requiring sign-in are unsupported by this adapter; it sends no authentication credential.

Startup schedules discovery immediately after storage is ready. Saving, enabling or changing a
connection also attempts it immediately, then an enabled gateway refreshes every five minutes
without Settings being open. **Refresh Ollama models** beside the model list requests a refresh
and coalesces with one already running. A connection save remains saved when discovery fails;
the returned discovery state explains the failure. Disabling or stopping cancels scheduled
discovery. Saving the connection off also blocks all new Ollama HTTP work and closes open gateway
discovery/preflight/inference requests; work already accepted by the remote server may continue.
No unload/remote-stop request is sent. A response/status from a prior connection revision cannot
overwrite the current catalog or discovery status.

Discovery reads `/api/tags` and bounded `/api/show` metadata. A complete snapshot reconciles the
catalog atomically. A partial/failed scan preserves the previous complete snapshot and last
success time; a successful empty list marks previously known models missing. Scans are bounded to
256 models, four concurrent detail reads, five seconds per metadata request, thirty seconds per
scan and 2 MiB per response. Cached details are invalidated when their digest or connection changes.
These operations never generate text, load/unload a model or change owner defaults.

Discovered rows use the exact server-reported names, namespaces and tags and remain harness-managed:
the owner can enable/disable them, not edit their metadata or delete them. A newly supported model
starts enabled; refreshes preserve the owner's enabled preference, stored selections and defaults.
Missing or unsupported rows remain visible with their availability reason. They cannot start new
runs, but reappearance can restore availability without losing that preference. Availability and
enablement are separate: `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` is not `MODEL_DISABLED`. Catalog, picker, publication
and runtime resolution read the same availability facts. A server outage does not erase the last
complete catalog; service readiness can still block a run. A model removed between discovery and
dispatch fails visibly without substitution or an automatic pull. The recorded digest is discovery
metadata, not a guarantee that an Ollama tag always points to immutable weights.

After startup migrations, current connection state governs public/runtime catalog reads. Off projects **Ollama is off
in Settings**, and metadata from a different/absent connection revision projects **Not yet listed
at the new address**. Both use unavailable `missing` state while preserving the snapshot and
owner Enabled choice. An address change does not pretend old models were checked at the new
origin; only a complete current enabled-revision scan restores availability. Failed scans retain
usable last-complete availability only within the same revision, never across origins.

An explicit structurally valid Ollama process model in `GG_DEFAULTS.byHarness.ollama` defers
catalog-dependent validation, so first startup and later offline/missing/unsupported-model
restarts keep Settings available for correction. JSON/schema/effort-enum validation still applies;
an effort-only process default without a model is unresolved. A model-only default stays partial,
with no implicit effort. Owner/loop default authoring keeps its usual validation. The actual
selected inference still requires the exact enabled/available model and supported effort before
publication/admission/execution; an absent Ollama row is restorable `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` until
discovery succeeds. No startup generation, synchronous remote probe, default substitution or
default rewrite is introduced. Codex/Claude process-default refusal semantics are unchanged.

For an existing current-format store, startup validates process defaults read-only against the
established catalog before mutable storage or additive migrations. This early view needs no
discovery tables; normal discovery-aware reads begin after migration. Existing Codex/Claude
refusals still happen before database writes, and a normal upgrade needs no reset or format conversion.

### Supported inference controls

This increment supports text and structured JSON in **fresh** conversations only. It supports no
tools/tool calls, plugins, MCP, context-file reads, web search, images or native audio. Use
`session.policy: 'fresh'`, `sandbox: 'read-only'` and `approval: 'never'`; capabilities, raw config
overrides and context files must be empty, and tool network/web-search flags must be false.
Those policy labels describe a tool-free model request, not OS confinement of the Ollama server.
Chat's explicit bounded history makes multi-turn Chat possible with a fresh request per turn;
audio first passes through the configured workflow normalizer and reaches Ollama as text.

Effort choices come from detected capabilities rather than the Codex effort table:

| Reported capability                                                             | Offered control                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| No thinking capability                                                          | `none`; omit `think`                            |
| Thinking metadata explicitly supports `false`                                   | `none` maps to `think: false`                   |
| Named values exactly matching `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`           | The identical canonical name                    |
| Absent/null thinking metadata, with the supported Qwen3.5 server family profile | `none` maps to `think: false`                   |
| Thinking capability without a supported explicit false/named control or profile | Unavailable, with an unsupported-control reason |

An on/off-only model offers `none` when false is explicit; `true` and unknown names are not renamed
to invented intensity levels. The catalog prefers `none` as its default when available, then an
exact supported reported default, then its first supported canonical level. This is catalog
guidance, not permission to select a model or overwrite owner defaults. Configure a model and
supported effort at the node, loop or inherited owner/process defaults as usual. The adapter
rechecks its proven control metadata before dispatch.

The bounded Qwen3.5 profile requires server-reported `qwen35` family (or explicit `qwen3.5`
renderer) plus completion/thinking capabilities; it is never guessed from a model-name substring.
Explicit thinking metadata takes precedence. Other unknown thinking-capable families without
supported controls remain unavailable. This profile follows the official
[boolean thinking API](https://ollama.com/blog/thinking) and
[Qwen3.5 renderer behavior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/model/renderers/qwen35_test.go).

### Readiness, completion and recovery

Ollama preflight is a bounded service/protocol probe without generation. A ready result does not
prove every model fits the server's memory or has completed a turn; service failures use service
connection guidance rather than CLI installation/login instructions. In the system/CLI diagnostic,
unused unavailable/off Ollama is a warning; an explicit Ollama process model makes an unavailable
service a failed diagnostic. Its default-model check awaits discovery when unknown, then checks
known availability, Enabled and exact effort. An explicit Ollama process model with no Codex
process-default entry also makes unavailable Codex a warning and omits its undefined-model check;
other Codex/Claude checks retain their existing policy. These reports do not become a startup or
run-admission gate; selected-node readiness remains authoritative.

CLI preflight reads a saved Ollama connection without writes only from a current, fully migrated
readable store. For an existing pending/unsupported/unreadable store it defers the Ollama probe
with a warning and no HTTP, rather than guessing environment settings over an unread saved Off
choice. A genuinely missing database, or a missing connection row in a current store, may use
environment defaults. Preflight never initializes that row or starts discovery.

Inference requires a terminal
`done: true` frame. Malformed/truncated streams, server errors, unexpected tool calls and missing
terminal completion fail without promoting partial content to a reply. Thinking content is never
the final answer. Frames are bounded to 1 MiB and total streamed/final content to 8 MiB. Usage comes
from terminal counters; missing counters are zero rather than estimates. Native JSON Schema
format support still passes through engine validation.

The local `ollama:<id>` handle correlates native evidence; it is not a resumable provider session.
Authored `resume-own`, `resume-previous`, `resume-named` and enabled same-session schema repair are
rejected. `resume` reports `HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING`; existing explicit **Start fresh** recovery is
the available action. Invalid structured output fails normally. A transport failure after dispatch
may be delivery-uncertain and is never automatically repeated. Cancellation closes the request and
reader; it does not claim remote computation stopped or unload the model. Node/run deadlines
remain the generation limits, without a hidden total generation timeout. An origin/revision change
cannot retarget or abort a model turn already dispatched; new/unsubmitted work checks the current
revision before dispatch. Explicit owner disable closes open requests with truthful delivery
state, without a remote-stop guarantee. See
[ADR-0066](decisions/ADR-0066-native-ollama-and-model-discovery.md).

## No-turn readiness (#179)

For Codex and Claude, readiness describes CLI prerequisites, independently of catalog enablement. `ready` confirms
version, required CLI flags and local login only; it never promises account access to a model.
The `models` field lists adapter identities and efforts, even when the CLI is not ready.
No probe sends a prompt, creates a session, or checks entitlement through inference.
Ollama instead probes its configured HTTP service as described above; it has no CLI/login prerequisite.

| State                 | Meaning and next action                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checking` (web only) | No result exists yet. A recheck keeps the last result instead; this is not a server readiness result.                                                                                     |
| `unknown`             | Timeout, cancellation, empty/unrecognized login output (even after exit 0) or another inconclusive probe. Login stays unestablished. Check the CLI and retry; model support is undecided. |
| `ready`               | Required CLI capabilities and local authentication passed; account model access remains untested.                                                                                         |
| `cli-missing`         | Executable not found. Install it or correct the configured binary path, then retry.                                                                                                       |
| `cli-incompatible`    | Version or required CLI capability failed verification. Update the installed CLI and retry.                                                                                               |
| `auth`                | Positive sign-out, wrong Claude account method or authentication-error evidence, including explicit HTTP/API 401/403. Run `claude auth login` or `codex login`, then retry.               |
| `quota`               | Explicit HTTP/API 429 or allowance/rate-limit diagnostic, even beside incidental network advice. Check account allowance and retry when permitted; preserve the model.                    |
| `transport`           | Explicit connection or temporary provider-service failure. Check connectivity/service status and retry; preserve the model.                                                               |

Only user-disabled models (`MODEL_DISABLED`) or identities absent from GraphGoblin support
(`MODEL_NOT_IN_CATALOG`) mean model unavailable.
A failed catalog fetch is unknown, not removal. An effort or wrong-harness configuration error
is reported separately. This change adds no retirement, substitution or usage-recovery behavior.

Claude probes its configured executable (default `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe`) in a
fresh empty directory: version (minimum 2.1.285), help with the hidden `--max-turns` parser check,
and local auth status. Help must advertise every launch flag, including `--model` and `--effort`.
Codex probes the SDK-bundled CLI or `GG_CODEX_BINARY`: version (minimum SDK baseline 0.160.0),
`exec --help`, `exec resume --help`, then `login status`, also in a fresh empty directory.
The exec help must advertise `--json`, `--model`, `--sandbox`, `--cd`, `--skip-git-repo-check`,
`--output-schema`, and `--config` (the SDK uses the latter for reasoning effort and policy).
Each command has a 15-second deadline; neither command includes a prompt. Advertised flags
establish syntax only; runtime verification still owns model/effort execution truth.

Draft create, template-draft create, import and save validate catalog/configuration only: they
never probe CLI readiness or wait for a provider prerequisite. Readiness cannot reject a draft.
The editor obtains readiness separately from `/harness/preflight`.
Explicit validate, publish, preflight and manual API/MCP trigger start use an operation-owned memo.
Each referenced harness is probed once per operation, including failures and multiple nodes;
distinct harnesses are probed concurrently. Concurrent requests own separate memos; nothing is
retained on the container or module. Run admission pins the checked version and rejects failed
prerequisites before starting a turn. Readiness issues use `HARNESS_READINESS_<STATE>` (hyphens
become underscores); catalog/configuration issues retain their existing codes.

Claude's ready `models` list also constrains the effective model and effort (#205). Manual
admission resolves each pinned inference/LLM selection with the run's pinned owner/process
defaults and its definition's loop defaults, rejecting `EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED` on the node before
recording the run. Request resolution in the engine checks the catalog before every adapter
request (manual and automatic starts, subloop children, resumes and recovery) and does not probe
the CLI per request: Claude's catalog rows are seeded from the adapter's own capability table, so
the catalog check enforces the same efforts. An unknown or unready probe retains the existing
readiness handling; no capability check substitutes a model or effort or claims provider
entitlement. The editor intersects the same ready capabilities with the catalog's effort choices.

Manual UI/API/MCP trigger start checks the engine's frozen root definition (published version or
draft snapshot) and every executable pinned subloop definition, recursively. Both `latest` and
numbered child references use the published records the engine prepared for this start, never a
child's draft or a publication that arrives while a probe is pending. A breadth-first walk visits
each version once at its shallowest depth, protects cycles and applies the execution handler's
configured subloop depth limit (or that node's override, at most 64). Harnesses shared by parent
and children share one probe; distinct harnesses are probed concurrently. An unready descendant
returns 422 `HARNESS_NOT_READY`, with the child loop name, loop/version ids and node id in its
issues, before any parent run, queued event, draft snapshot or mutation is committed.
The engine commits the same checked intent after probing and revalidates that its versions still
exist; slow probes do not hold the shared admission/deletion lock.

Replay, scheduled and webhook admissions, internally started subloops and resumes do not gain
this manual trigger-start preflight; their existing execution checks remain in place and can
fail after earlier nodes have run. In particular, replay can return 202 with an unready harness,
execute preceding mutations, then fail when it reaches that harness. Unresolved child references
retain their existing `SUBLOOP_NOT_FOUND` execution behavior. Readiness is an admission-time
observation, not a guarantee of later account access.

`/harness/preflight` exposes seven server states. `checking` is a web-only request state.
`authenticated` is absent if login was not checked or could not be established; false requires
positive signed-out evidence. Claude parses auth-status JSON even on
exit 1 (`loggedIn:false` or an explicit nonempty non-Claude.ai account method). During auth status,
explicit `Not logged in` text on stdout or bounded stderr confirms sign-out even on exit 0.
Empty output, `{}` or an unrecognised login response on exit 0 is `unknown`, with no `authenticated` field;
a successful exit alone establishes no login fact. A recognised Claude.ai status or Codex
"Logged in" status establishes true; an explicit signed-out status establishes false.

No-turn diagnostic precedence is CLI-syntax errors first, explicit HTTP/API 401/403 (`auth`),
429 (`quota`) or 5xx (`transport`) next, then connection errors/wording, then quota/auth keywords.
Thus incidental "network" advice cannot override 401 or 429, while connection errors such as
`ECONNREFUSED` still outrank incidental auth words in server/refresh diagnostics. Version numbers
are not HTTP status evidence. For Claude's unstructured diagnostics, recognised stderr wins
over conflicting stdout because stderr is the CLI's primary error channel; stdout is consulted
when stderr is absent or classified `unknown`, so an unrelated warning cannot hide stdout quota.
Positive Claude auth-status sign-out evidence (structured or explicit text) is handled separately;
process start, timeout, cancellation, overflow and unconfirmed termination remain authoritative.
Lost check output comes next: a check whose stdout or stderr could not be read infers no state,
sign-out included, from what it captured (#364).
None of this inference applies to
model-turn stdout or changes turn retry eligibility.
Harness checks in `/system/preflight` carry state alongside the system's `ok`/`warn`/`fail`
severity. Each problem is one detail sentence and one action ending "then retry preflight"
(`readinessMessage` in the domain package); a specific detail, such as the CLI version below the
minimum or the missing option, replaces the generic one rather than being followed by it.

## Codex adapter for 1.0 (Decided)

### Facts the design relies on

Verified on 2026-10-02 against the `openai/codex` repository and docs. Full notes in `research/codex-sdk.md`.

- `@openai/codex-sdk` is Apache-2.0 and requires Node 18 or newer. It is pinned exactly at 0.160.0. It depends on `@openai/codex` at the same version, which ships the native CLI, and by default runs that bundled binary (the adapter's `codexBinary` option overrides it). It exchanges JSONL events with the CLI over stdio.
- Threads persist under `~/.codex/sessions` and can be resumed with `resumeThread(id, options)`.
- `run` and `runStreamed` accept an `outputSchema` for structured output and an AbortSignal.
- `runStreamed` yields `thread.started`, `turn.started`, `item.started|updated|completed`, `turn.completed` (usage), `turn.failed`, and `error` events.
- The client accepts `codexPathOverride`, `env`, `baseUrl`, `apiKey`, `config` (flattened to dotted `--config` keys), and `configOverrides` (raw `key=value` strings). Thread options are `model`, `modelReasoningEffort`, `sandboxMode`, `approvalPolicy`, `networkAccessEnabled`, `webSearchMode`, `webSearchEnabled`, `workingDirectory`, `skipGitRepoCheck`, `additionalDirectories`, and `threadSource`.
- Reasoning effort values used are `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max` (`model_reasoning_effort`), as the CLI's own model catalog lists them per model (see "Model catalog").
- Codex has a native Windows sandbox since March 2026, and plugins bundling skills, MCP servers, and connectors since CLI 0.117.0.

All of this was verified against the pinned version in M4; `research/codex-sdk.md` lists every option with the CLI argument it becomes.

### Authentication (Decided)

GraphGoblin uses the machine's existing Codex login, which may be a ChatGPT subscription. It never stores or proxies Codex credentials. The adapter's `preflight` runs the CLI to confirm it is installed and authenticated, and the settings page shows the result. If an API key is desired later, it is passed through `env`, never persisted by GraphGoblin.

### Mapping inference config to the SDK (Decided, verified in M4)

An enabled GraphGoblin catalogue entry or a ready preflight does not establish that the selected
model is available to the API process user's actual Codex login and provider endpoint. Preflight
checks installation, supported CLI capabilities and authentication without requesting a model turn.
The bundled CLI's static model/plan metadata is not a live entitlement check. The October 2026
ChatGPT-account refusal for `gpt-5.5` in [#427](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/427)
is dated evidence, not a universal current restriction or proof that an API key always fixes it.

For a Codex inference turn's structured HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`, the adapter keeps the provider's explanation
as `HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED`; the run records `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with that adapter code and
does not offer Resume. An account/endpoint explanation is evidence for that refused request,
not a diagnosis for every unavailable model or unknown provider error. Deliberately choose a
model supported for that login/endpoint, or change the login/endpoint as the API process user;
correct the applicable definition/default, restart the API if process defaults changed, and start a new run. GraphGoblin does not substitute
another model or globally disable a seed from one account's refusal. See
[model-access troubleshooting](guide/07-troubleshooting.md#codex-model-unavailable-for-this-account-or-endpoint).

LLM decisions deliberately omit provider text: the same refusal maps to `DECIDER_HTTP_ERROR`
and a non-resumable `EVALUATION_PROVIDER_FAILED` with “Decision provider request failed.”
That run record cannot establish an account-specific cause. Diagnose the selected decision
model/login/endpoint separately; this change does not expand the decision's diagnostic boundary.

The adapter sends the supported thread settings below explicitly on every session. Their SDK CLI arguments follow `config` overrides and win over the corresponding keys in `configOverrides` or `config.toml`. Other keys, including Windows sandbox backend selection, remain inherited unless overridden. This precedence alone does not establish the enforcement effect of every other sandbox-related key.

Codex turns inherit the user's configured plugins, including their enabled/disabled state and plugin-provided tools/services ([ADR-0067](decisions/ADR-0067-codex-inherits-configured-plugins.md)). No default `features.plugins` override is injected. An inference node opts out of all plugins by adding `"features":{"plugins":false}` to its existing `harnessOptions.configOverrides`; this includes resumes and same-session output-schema repairs. An explicit `true` can override a user feature disable while respecting individually disabled plugins. Individual plugin IDs contain `@` and cannot pass the node override key validation.

LLM decisions and `coerce`/output-transform repairs use separate structured calls with no node overrides. Their current callers supply no working directory, so those calls start in a fresh temporary directory and inherit user/global Codex configuration, not the caller's inference override or trusted-project layer. Disable the plugin feature or an individual plugin in effective user/global configuration to exclude it from those calls; this also changes ordinary Codex sessions. There is no per-node structured-call plugin opt-out.

Other extension isolation remains ([ADR-0063](decisions/ADR-0063-loop-turns-without-personal-extensions.md)). Before each turn the adapter runs `codex mcp list --json` in the turn's working directory **with plugins switched off only for discovery**, so plugin-owned servers are not listed and then suppressed. It starts the turn with every listed standalone MCP server disabled (`mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false`), with `features.apps`, `features.memories`, `features.hooks`, `features.multi_agent` (sub-agent spawning) and `features.goals` false, and with `notify=[]`. If the listing fails, the turn does not start. Plain `--config` overrides cannot clear a table such as `mcp_servers={}`, because the CLI merges them into the loaded configuration; standalone servers are therefore disabled by name and remain available through explicit node overrides.

Configuration errors reported by the CLI retain their pre-submission refusal. Plugin inheritance follows normal CLI resolution, rather than checking package health: pinned CLI 0.160.0 silently skips unknown plugin IDs and missing plugin MCP files. A successful turn does not prove every configured plugin loaded. System preflight adds an informational `plugins.codex` warning after Codex CLI/login readiness succeeds, and Settings shows the same scope notice in the Codex card (#442): loaded plugin tools are not verified by this check. Readiness, authentication, normal inheritance and node overrides remain unchanged. The notice starts no inventory, app-server or provider probe. Supported CLI inventory can help investigate, but configuration and tool lists do not establish complete loaded-plugin health; see [missing Codex tools](guide/07-troubleshooting.md#codex-plugin-tools-are-missing).

Every listed server name and every segment of a node's override key must be one plain TOML key (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), and not `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`. The shared contract checks raw authored keys before record parsing, including dotted keys, nested tables and tables inside arrays. The editor and API reject an invalid key with its field path instead of discarding it; publication also checks retained drafts and reports `CODEX_CONFIG_KEY_INVALID` on the inference node. Ordinary scalar values, valid tables and dotted keys keep their existing behavior. A previously stored invalid-key draft remains unchanged when publication is refused. Such stored definitions must be corrected before restarting with this contract, because the existing store guard refuses invalid definitions (see the CHANGELOG upgrade note).

A listed server name that breaks this rule refuses the turn with `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` (resumable once the machine's configuration is fixed). The adapter independently checks overrides with the same key rule and refuses them with `HARNESS_INVALID_CONFIGURATION`. The run records this as a non-resumable `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` with that adapter code, so the node must change. Both are definitely not submitted. Existing HTTP reserved-key guards continue to apply before contract validation.

API request-schema paths preserve literal authored member names with RFC 6901 escaping, including
`/` and `~` and nested array positions ([API error responses](07-api-and-streaming.md#error-responses-decided)).
Recovery of a manually edited stored row needs more than removing its bad override key: if its
defaulted harness was omitted, explicitly store `harness: "codex"` in the node configuration as
part of the operator correction on the stopped target store, alongside the key repair. Normal
API writes already materialize that value. Startup and input-schema validation do not rewrite a
stored omission; key-only repair can allow startup while GET and publication still fail. The
CHANGELOG recipe identifies the target and full backup procedure, limits any copy rehearsal to
offline checks without a gateway, and requires both discovery queries plus exact stored-text
readback because SQLite's affected-row count alone does not prove a quoted member changed. Before
restart, correct applicable editable rows, resolve invalid-key discovery results and choose a
deliberate disposition for any actually incompatible snapshots. An omitted harness alone in an
immutable snapshot is accepted by definition parsing. An explicit version read of that manually
authored snapshot can still return `500 RESPONSE_INVALID`. Preserve its history.
If recovery uses a fresh store, adopt that store's configuration and credentials and use the loop
ID returned by import. An incompatible snapshot still blocks the original database. After the
operator starts the chosen store for normal service, authenticated read-only GET verifies
its served draft/current definitions; offline checks cover other retained versions. Verification
does not publish owner drafts or start runs. Publication and restart tests use separate synthetic
fixtures with fake harnesses and timers disabled, not a copy of the owner's store. No runtime
converter or backfill is provided (ADR-0062).

### Event normalisation (Decided)

| Codex event                                                       | `HarnessEvent`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `thread.started`                                                  | `session` with `mode: 'fresh'`, as soon as it arrives. On resume, emit resumed mode only after the native ID matches and the turn succeeds.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `item.completed`                                                  | `item`; `agent_message` → `message`, `reasoning`, `command_execution` → `command`, `file_change` → `file-change`, `mcp_tool_call` → `tool-call`, `web_search` → `search`, `error`, anything else → `other`, each with a one-line summary and the raw item (command output capped at 16 KiB) as `detail` |
| `item.started`, `item.updated`                                    | not emitted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| SDK item `status`                                                 | Explicit `completed`, `failed`, and in-progress/running states normalize to `ok`, `failed`, and `running`. Command items also derive status from integer `exit_code` when present; every command has a status. Other item types include status only when the SDK reports one.                           |
| `command_execution` fields                                        | Normalized command items carry a one-line `commandPreview` (max `COMMAND_PREVIEW_MAX`, currently 160 chars), an optional integer `exitCode`, and a required status. The bounded summary is independent of these fields, so a long command cannot hide its exit code.                                    |
| `turn.completed`                                                  | `usage` (`input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_output_tokens`), then `turn-complete`                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `turn.failed`, thrown SDK error, stream ending without completion | `error { code, message, retriable }`, and `result` rejects with the same `code`                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

An `error` item, such as a configuration deprecation warning, is an ordinary item and never fails a turn. A top-level `error` event only counts if the turn then fails. Codes: `HARNESS_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` (HTTP 429, usage limit, quota; retriable only for plain rate limits), `HARNESS_NOT_AUTHENTICATED` (401, 403, not logged in), `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` (binary not found), `HARNESS_TRANSPORT_FAILED` (5xx and stream disconnects), `HARNESS_ARGUMENTS_REJECTED` (the CLI rejected its arguments, or the provider refused the turn's request itself with HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`, for example an effort the model does not accept; the message keeps the provider's text and names the refused parameter), and `HARNESS_TURN_FAILED` (other failures). The engine preserves quota and transport causes at run level; submission provenance separately controls whether any retry is safe.

When the CLI fails a turn it reports the failure in the event stream (`error`, then `turn.failed`) and then exits with code 1; the SDK then throws `Codex Exec exited with code 1: <stderr>`, and the CLI's stderr is usually only its startup banner (`Reading prompt from stdin...`). That thrown error is read as the stderr evidence it carries, piece by piece: a stderr that is one structured provider error as a whole, or else each line, read from the structured provider error it holds (also after a prefix such as `ERROR: `) and as text otherwise, so a repeated provider error never reaches a message heuristic. A piece that exactly repeats evidence the stream reported (code, message, retry flag and submission metadata) adds nothing, whatever rank its text would get. Every other typed piece joins the evidence fold in order, so a later refusal, an authentication failure or a missing session beside a repeat is ranked like any other evidence. When nothing new and typed remains, the wrapper adds nothing if the stream reported the turn's failure, which includes fatal stream evidence (`turn.failed`, a terminal or pinned error) also after `turn.completed`; otherwise the wrapper is the cause (#243, PR #426 audit scans 2 and 3). Only that exact SDK error is treated as a wrapper (a plain `Error` reading `Codex Exec exited with code <n>:` or `… with signal <name>:`); any other thrown error, such as the SDK's `Failed to parse item: …` for a line that is not JSON, joins the evidence fold as usual. The provider's refusal is recognised from the parsed `status` and `error.type` before any message heuristic, so provider text that happens to contain a CLI phrase such as `invalid value` or `Thread not found` stays the provider's refusal (#243, [F2 LP-5 defect D2](qa/2026-10-27-final-f2-live/README.md), [fix record](qa/2026-10-27-f2-fixes/README.md)).

Inference `node.progress` uses a strict item variant for each normalized type (`message`, `reasoning`, `command`, `file-change`, `tool-call`, `search`, `error`, and `other`): each has an id, summary (max 2,000 chars), and only allowlisted fields. Commands include a required `status` (`ok`, `failed`, or `running`), optional bounded `commandPreview` (max `COMMAND_PREVIEW_MAX`, currently 160 chars), and optional integer `exitCode`. Other item types may include the normalized status when the SDK supplies one. Error summaries are replaced with a fixed label, tool-call diagnostics are omitted, and progress never includes `detail` or command output. Script progress is a separate strict shape: integer `exitCode`, `stderr` capped at 2,000 chars, and nonnegative integer `stdoutBytes`. This build does not rewrite command items from retired formats or retain a conversion audit; unsupported stores require an explicit reset under ADR-0042.

### Cancellation (Decided, verified on Windows)

`cancel()` and the caller's AbortSignal both abort the signal passed to `runStreamed`. The SDK hands it to `child_process.spawn`, which kills the CLI. The SDK keeps the child process private, so the adapter cannot reach its pid for a `taskkill /T /F`. It does not need to on Windows: a live test (`LIVE=1`) starts a `workspace-write` session running `Start-Sleep -Seconds 120`, confirms the sleeping process exists, cancels, and confirms nothing with the marker survives, because Codex runs commands inside a job object that ends with the CLI. The same was observed with `danger-full-access`. `result` rejects with an `AbortError` once the CLI's output ends.

The SDK's event stream ends only when the CLI's stdout closes. A process the CLI started can hold that pipe after the kill, so the adapter waits at most `cancelGraceMs` (5 s, the ADR-0049 harness acknowledgement) after the abort. If the output is still open then, the turn fails `HARNESS_TERMINATION_UNCONFIRMED` (non-retriable, `delivery-uncertain`) and `cancel()` rejects with the same code, as for the Claude harness; an explicit force therefore ends in `force-failed`. The adapter cannot end that process itself (ADR-0049 N10). POSIX behaviour is unverified on the development machine.

### Codex structured completions and decider

`CodexStructured` (`StructuredPort`) starts one fresh thread per call with the schema,
sandbox `read-only`, approval `never`, no command network access and no web search, in the request's
working directory or an empty temporary directory it removes afterwards. It returns
parsed JSON (or raw text for a non-JSON reply) for the engine to validate.

The request's working directory takes precedence over the adapter's configured directory;
neither configured directory is removed. Without either, the adapter exclusively creates a
short random-suffix scratch directory with `mkdir`, avoiding `mkdtemp`'s lower Windows path
limit. It makes at most four attempts (three retries) on `EEXIST`; other creation errors propagate before the
harness starts. A colliding directory is never reused or removed, and cleanup belongs only
to a directory this call created. Cancellation and primary failures keep their existing
cleanup precedence. The pinned SDK separately writes the required output schema under the
host temporary root. Its managed patch shortens that directory's native `mkdtemp` prefix
from `codex-output-schema-` to `gg-schema-`, keeping its allocation and cleanup semantics
([ADR-0087](decisions/ADR-0087-short-codex-schema-temp-prefix.md)). Real-SDK/harmless-CLI
tests at the measured 226-character Windows temporary root observe a 249-character adapter
scratch, 243-character SDK schema directory and 255-character schema file, with normal,
error and abort cleanup. These controlled fixtures are not a provider turn or a promise of
arbitrary long-path support; ordinary OS/CLI limits still apply.

Configured plugins are inherited through the common harness, including their tools; the
read-only sandbox controls local commands rather than the authority of plugin services.
The engine's LLM decision and coerce-repair callers supply neither a working directory
nor node config overrides, so these calls use the fresh-directory/user-configuration
behavior described above. Their service calls are not guaranteed to be side-effect free.
`CodexDecider` (`DeciderPort`, `id: 'codex'`) asks for `{ route, confidence, reasoning }`,
where route is an enum of declared route IDs. Schemas follow strict structured-output
rules; the adapter validates the entire answer and confidence bounds without clamping
or coercion. It is always `available()`; harness health is reported by `preflight`.

The engine enforces the run's pinned `settings.structuredTimeoutMs` around LLM decision
evaluations and output-transform repairs through `StructuredPort`. Inference output-schema
repairs instead run on the node's own `HarnessPort` session and follow its explicit
`timeoutSeconds` and the run deadline; this completion limit does not bound them. Omission/null means Unlimited; a finite authored value is milliseconds
per completion, not a usage budget. The Loop tab, Settings defaults and inspector
expose it. `CodexStructured` checks abort before acquiring resources and again before
starting, passes the signal into the harness/SDK call, explicitly cancels the session
on abort and removes its temporary directory after cancellation cleanup. It never
adds its own hidden completion deadline. The engine returns the typed
`STRUCTURED_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT` without waiting forever for a port that ignores abort;
late fulfillments and non-abort rejections are logged once and cannot reach the run's thread.
Decision and structured-port repair timeouts include provider, resolved model and effort
in `details.provenance`. Explicit Cancel
remains cancellation, and an authored run deadline retains its own failure code.
See [ADR-0051](decisions/ADR-0051-structured-completion-deadlines.md).

### Wiring

```ts
import { CodexDecider, createCodexAdapters } from '@graphgoblin/adapter-codex';

const codex = createCodexAdapters({
  logger,
  model: settings.defaults.byHarness.codex?.model,
  effort: settings.defaults.byHarness.codex?.effort,
});
const structured = codex.structured; // Or an injected StructuredPort.
const decider = new CodexDecider(structured);
// ports: harnesses: { codex: codex.harness }, structured,
//        deciders: [decider], classifiers: classifierRegistry
```

The API additionally supplies `ports.classifiers: ClassifierRegistryPort`. Classifier decisions and exit predicates use `resolve(ownerId, catalogId, primitive)` and check the requested capability before dispatch. Codex supplies the structured LLM evaluator; the separate exit judge facade is removed. The registry creates SDK or HTTP clients from immutable configuration snapshots, invalidates them on catalog/referenced-secret writes and deletes, and rechecks metadata and usable secrets on every resolution. An in-flight request keeps its snapshot; subsequent decisions see the edit.

### Context injection (Decided)

A harness cannot accept conversation history as messages. The thread reaches Codex through three channels, all configured on the inferencing node:

1. **Prompt template.** The default template renders the trigger summary, selected variables, the last N messages, and `lastOutput`. Input transforms shape the view the template sees.
2. **Context files.** Optional files written under the working directory before the session starts, from templates. The default location is `.graphgoblin/context/<nodeId>.md` and the default prompt mentions it. GraphGoblin never edits the user's own `AGENTS.md`.
3. **Session resume.** The harness keeps its own history. A resumed turn receives an explicit prompt: a new authored task under its configured policy, a retained definitely-unsubmitted task, or the continuation prompt for uncertain work. See submission markers and recovery below.

### Own-session continuity (#33)

`resume-own` is opt-in; the default stays `fresh`. It uses the same adapter resume
path and complete per-turn settings as previous/named selection. Its handle is scoped
to one node/run/harness. The durable log identifies the latest completed visit's exact
attempt row; no adapter-local memory or new storage schema is required. A new adapter
instance after restart can resume that persisted native ID. Replay forks and child
runs have independent IDs/logs and start fresh.

An optional `resetAfterVisits` (positive safe integer, 1 to 9,007,199,254,740,991;
omitted means never automatically reset) starts a new provider conversation after N
completed logical visits. Retries and repairs do not count as extra visits. It never
clears the main-loop thread. Existing prompt templates, input transforms and context
files deliberately supply the current loop context to either fresh or resumed turns.
Fresh conversation isolation does not change the authored working-directory/tool policy.

Missing sessions remain `HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING`, non-resumable, without a silent
fresh fallback. A prior visit's own handle, like previous/named handles, is not proof
that a new authored task was submitted. #244/ADR-0045's acceptance and exact-task retry
rules apply unchanged; #265 provides the explicit recovery choice below.

### Structured output and repair (Decided)

Codex enforces `outputSchema` natively. GraphGoblin still validates the parsed result against the schema. On failure, the configurable repair policy applies: up to `maxAttempts` extra turns on the same session with a repair prompt that quotes the validation errors, then either `fail-run` with code `OUTPUT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` or `continue-raw`. The same `RepairPolicy` type is used by the `coerce` mutation operation.

### Usage recording (Decided)

Usage reported by the harness is written to `harness.usage` events and rolled into `counters.usage`. It is informational. No limits, warnings, or budgets are derived from it.

### Output handling (Decided)

- Transcript: the full item list is stored as an artifact of kind `transcript` when `captureTranscript` is `artifact`.
- Messages: `final` appends one assistant message with the final text. `final-and-notes` also appends short notes for file changes and commands run, tagged `harness-note`, which later truncation and drop operations can target.
- Output transforms run before messages are appended, so redaction and truncation apply to what enters the thread.

### Model catalog (Decided)

There are two catalogs: `model_catalog` is the harness LLM catalog described below; `classifier_models` is an owner-scoped catalog of Choice/classification, Noul, and Score capabilities, with provider model ids, API roots, and optional secret references. The `model_catalog` table carries `source: 'harness' | 'litellm'` and `enabled`. Harness entries are enable/disable only, using PATCH; their metadata cannot be edited or deleted through the API. ### Windows notes

The product owner develops on Windows 11. Codex's native Windows sandbox applies. POSIX signals are not available, so process trees are killed with `taskkill /T /F` where GraphGoblin owns the process (scripts); for Codex sessions the CLI's own job object ends the tree on abort (see "Cancellation"). Every provider and tool process starts with `windowsHide: true` and piped stdio, which gives it its own hidden console: Codex preflight, Claude turns and probes, scripts, and Codex sessions. The SDK 0.160.0 spawns sessions without the option, so a pnpm patch adds it (ADR-0049 acceptance amendment); without it the CLI shared the gateway's console and a terminal Ctrl+C killed a running turn. Paths are normalised with `node:path` and never built by string concatenation.

Windows starts no process whose working directory is missing or longer than 258 characters (error 267). Node reports that refusal as spawn `ENOENT`, the code of a missing executable; the Claude adapter's [start refusals](#claude-code-adapter-26) say which operand it could establish (#364). Codex 0.160.0 reports that for a worker command as `CreateProcessWithLogonW failed: 267` (elevated sandbox) or `CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 267` (unelevated). The #102 occurrences came from per-command directories the worker model mistyped, not from GraphGoblin's `--cd`. The Claude and Codex adapters create their `gg-claude-probe-*` and `gg-codex-probe-*` check directories with `mkdir`, because Windows `fs.mkdtemp` fails from 248 characters (247 still works); a name that already exists is never reused or removed, and up to four fresh names are tried. Evidence and the launch comparison matrix: [WP-F5 launch diagnosis](qa/2026-10-19-wp-f5-launch-diagnosis.md).

## Codex as a decider and a repair engine (Decided)

LLM decisions send rendered Liquid instructions, `{id,label}` route declarations, prepared context and resolved model/effort to `DeciderPort.route`. Exactly `route`, `confidence` and `reasoning` are required; the schema forbids additional properties and constrains route to submitted IDs. The adapter and engine check membership and finite confidence in [0,1]. Confidence is informational with no gate; reasoning is truncated to 2,048 characters. There is one completion, without repair or fallback. Separate `evaluateBoolean` requests serve temporary exit predicates.

LLM decisions and the `coerce` operation's output-transform repairs use fresh Codex structured threads with an output schema, a read-only command sandbox, approval `never`, no command network access and no web search. They inherit user/global plugins without the caller's node override or trusted-project layer. Inference output-schema repair instead continues on the inference node's own harness session and retains its options and working directory. These Codex calls use the installed account login; provider authentication and quota failures are reported normally. Plugin tools retain their service authority subject to CLI policy and service authentication: a read-only command sandbox guarantees neither no file changes through a service nor side-effect-free evaluation. Implemented by `CodexStructured` and `CodexDecider`, with inference repair on `HarnessPort`.

## Jev decider (Decided, M4)

Classifier decisions and exit predicates require an explicit `model` catalog id; choose `jev` for the built-in. Startup seeds that built-in before run recovery and refreshes its managed metadata without resetting enabled. Its fixed provider remains the pinned TypeSafe SDK, `jev-latest`, `https://api.typesafe.ai`, and `jev-api-key`. Exit predicates may select any enabled classifier supporting their declared primitive. Configuration status is a local usable-secret check, with no provider request; it does not establish reachability or valid provider authentication.

A fresh store seeds the local owner's encrypted `jev-api-key` secret from `GG_JEV_API_KEY`, or from `JEV_API_KEY` when `GG_JEV_API_KEY` is unset. An explicitly empty `GG_JEV_API_KEY` disables seeding, including the fallback; an existing secret is never overwritten. When seeding occurs, the startup log names the variable used: `seeded jev-api-key from GG_JEV_API_KEY` or `seeded jev-api-key from JEV_API_KEY`. The key value is never logged; without a non-empty seed or when the secret already exists, there is no seed log line.

`packages/adapter-jev` implements `DeciderPort` (`id: 'jev'`) over `@typesafe-ai/sdk` 0.6.0 (MIT, no dependencies). Choice, Noul and Score call `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` with a bearer key from the secret `jev-api-key`:

- `choose` sends the decision context as `state` and one `choice` question whose criteria map each stable option ID to its authored criterion. It returns the chosen stable option ID, the reported confidence (or that option's probability), and a probability map covering exactly the submitted option IDs. The engine compares classifier confidence with `minConfidence` and rejects a below-threshold answer with `EVALUATION_RESULT_REJECTED`, without fallback.
- `classifyNoul` sends a `noul` question with explicit `true` and `false` criteria and returns its true probability. The engine applies the authored truth threshold (default 0.5), then independently checks confidence in the selected side. Threshold equality passes.
- `score` sends an ordered array of rubric descriptions and preserves the fractional index, exact legend and available confidence/probabilities. The engine selects a stable authored band without rounding. Missing Score confidence is null; an authored minimum then fails with EVALUATION_INVALID_RESPONSE because its gate cannot be evaluated.

`available()` is synchronous: the decider resolves the key in the background at construction and caches a client; `init()` awaits that, and `refresh()` re-reads the secret. Without a key the chosen evaluator is unavailable and execution fails with restoration guidance. Failures carry codes: `DECIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `DECIDER_NOT_AUTHENTICATED` (401, 403), `DECIDER_RATE_LIMITED` (429), `DECIDER_HTTP_ERROR`, `DECIDER_UNREACHABLE`, and `DECIDER_INVALID_RESPONSE` (the response is validated with Zod). Jev Choice probabilities must cover exactly the submitted stable option IDs; unknown choices are invalid responses. Jev errors use fixed messages with only numeric HTTP status, and SDK logs use fixed summaries without provider text or response headers. Decision and exit-predicate failures share the engine's safe summaries; snapshots, paged events, and streams never retain provider error bodies or stacks. Engine provider warnings carry only safe name, code, status, and strategy metadata. Existing Choice calls retain SDK retries (twice for 408, 429 and 5xx by default). New Noul/Score calls explicitly disable retries and check cancellation before dispatch. The per-attempt timeout is 10 seconds; aborts surface as `AbortError`. The base URL and model are explicit options (`baseUrl`, default `https://api.typesafe.ai`; `model`, default `jev-latest`), never read from `TYPESAFE_*` environment variables.

## HTTP classifier endpoint contract (Decided, ADR-0021)

Register a custom entry with provider `http`, displayName, providerModel, nonempty unique primitives, an HTTP(S) API root without embedded credentials/query/fragment, and optional secretRef. Roots must not include the `/v1/systemone` request path, port 0, or whitespace (including encoded whitespace). When secretRef is supplied, HTTPS is required except for loopback hosts (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, or `[::1]`). New entries are disabled; metadata edits preserve enabled. The secret reference uses the Secrets name syntax and contains no credential value. HTTP execution supports Choice, Noul and Score; catalog capabilities filter editor choices and are rechecked at admission and dispatch.

The infrastructure HTTP client sends `POST {endpoint}/v1/systemone`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and `Authorization: Bearer <resolved secret>` only when secretRef is set:

```json
{
  "model": "kev-latest",
  "state": { "task": "Review the change" },
  "questions": {
    "answer": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "Which route?",
      "criteria": { "ship": "Ready to merge", "fix": "Needs work" }
    }
  }
}
```

Minimum response:

```json
{
  "answers": {
    "answer": {
      "type": "choice",
      "choice": "ship",
      "confidence": 0.8,
      "probabilities": { "ship": 0.8, "fix": 0.2 }
    }
  }
}
```

Probabilities must cover exactly every submitted label, and all probability/confidence values must be finite and in `[0,1]`. The selected choice must be one of the submitted labels; an undeclared choice produces `DECIDER_INVALID_RESPONSE` with fixed text that does not include the value. Omitted confidence uses the selected probability. Provider model/usage and additional provider metadata may accompany the response. Requests have a 10-second deadline and respect executor cancellation. Redirects are not followed: a 3xx produces `DECIDER_REDIRECT` with "Classifier redirects are not followed". Malformed JSON or invalid answers produce `DECIDER_INVALID_RESPONSE`; 401/403 (`DECIDER_NOT_AUTHENTICATED`), 429 (`DECIDER_RATE_LIMITED`), other HTTP errors (`DECIDER_HTTP_ERROR`), connection failures (`DECIDER_UNREACHABLE`), and timeouts (`DECIDER_TIMEOUT`) have fixed diagnostics, with no credential or untrusted provider body in them. Decision provider failures use typed `EVALUATION_*` failures and retain only safe transport diagnostics; cancellation retains its existing behaviour. Unavailable configuration, rejected classifier confidence and unknown selections produce the explicit typed decision failures described in docs/05; they never invoke a different evaluator. Malformed provider answers and transport text are not retained. A valid answer rejected only by confidence retains its validated canonical primitive facts, evaluator provenance and acceptance gate in failure details; it emits no `decision.made` event and selects no route. The registry passes the engine logger to decision-time Jev SDK clients so SDK retries and errors retain fixed log summaries without raw provider text.

Noul uses the same envelope with `questions.answer = { "type": "noul", "instructions": "Is it ready?", "criteria": { "true": "All checks pass", "false": "At least one check fails" } }`. Its response is `answers.answer = { "type": "noul", "noul": 0.8 }`, where `noul` is the true probability, not selected-side confidence.

Score sends `questions.answer = { "type": "score", "instructions": "Rate the result", "criteria": ["Incomplete", "Adequate", "Excellent"] }`. Its response is `answers.answer = { "type": "score", "score": 1.6, "legend": { "0": "Incomplete", "1": "Adequate", "2": "Excellent" } }`, optionally with finite confidence in `[0,1]` and probabilities keyed by every rubric index. The legend must exactly match the submitted rubric; the score must be finite and within `[0,N-1]`. Missing confidence/probabilities remain null. No alternate evaluator is called.

Kev-4B's owner recommends `kev.serve` on CUDA or Apple Silicon MLX; the protocol and Apache-2.0 licence were inspected in owner source, with evidence in [research/jev.md](research/jev.md#kev-http-protocol-verification-2026-10-05). GraphGoblin registers an existing service; it does not install or serve models. A different native protocol needs a bridge exposing this contract. Ordinary LiteLLM chat-completion routing does not supply Choice probabilities, so it is outside this classifier path.
